Standards Map.Intro to Swift App Development Reference: Use [Develop in Swift](https://developer.apple.com/tutorials/develop-in-swift/) to build a view. For a function such as `label(for:)`, read the call aloud and compare the argument label with the [Swift API Design Guidelines](https://www.swift.org/documentation/api-design-guidelines/). Use the [accessibility guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility/) to check what a control communicates at large text sizes and with VoiceOver. Before a simulated submission, compare the build and its metadata with the [App Review Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/).
Standards Map.Intro to Swift App Development Core Skil: SW1–SW3 take a view from source to a running app. SW4–SW7 give the displayed value a type, a stable identity and an owner. In SW8–SW12, trace a tap or a request from input through that owner to a changed screen. SW13–SW15 ask you to reproduce a failure and verify a repair across destinations and accessibility settings.
Standards Map.Intro to Swift App Development Next Topi: After SW20, choose a question your capstone left open. For example, would two devices need to share a record? Sketch how a conflict could arise from two offline edits. Cross-device sync adds backend and identity decisions beyond the local persistence taught in SW11.
Standards Map.Intro to Swift App Development Boundarie: The core projects use SwiftUI, supplied data and an iPhone simulator. SwiftData and Observation follow the iOS 17-or-later route. SW15–SW20 include written device and distribution cases. An authorized live distribution exercise is optional. SWX is an optional comparison with legacy drawing code.
Standards Map.Intro to Swift App Development Prerequis: Before editing a second screen, identify the target that builds the app (SW2), the type that owns the record (SW5) and the view that owns its editable state (SW7). In the [practice case](/course-assets/swift/intro-swift-practice-pack.md#state-and-data-flow-case), predict the stored value after Cancel and after Save. Compare each result with the [worked check](/course-assets/swift/intro-swift-verification-guide.md#state-and-data-flow-key).
Standards Map.Intro to Swift App Development Pathway M: Trace one dependency chain for a saved task. SW5 gives it a stable ID, SW7 separates the draft from saved state, SW10 edits the row by ID and SW11 checks it after relaunch. Mark the first step where two tasks with the same title could be confused. Use the [practice case](/course-assets/swift/intro-swift-practice-pack.md#lists-forms-and-crud-case) to test your answer.

Course Roadmap.Intro to Swift App Development Follow-Up: Work through SW1–SW14 to build and check local apps. SW15 supplies destination validation and SW16–SW18 explain distribution and signing. Bring one bounded user flow to SW19, then make a submit-or-hold decision in SW20. Shapes Studio is an optional geometry project.
Course Roadmap.Intro to Swift App Development Resource: For a first run, open [Mac Setup and Project Tooling](/courses#intro-to-swift-app-development-sw1-mac-setup-and-first-launch-intro-to-swift-app-development-sw1-mac-setup-and-first-launch-curriculum-core-project-mac-setup-and-project-tooling) and use one source role. For an offline prediction, use the [practice case](/course-assets/swift/intro-swift-practice-pack.md#mac-setup-and-first-launch-case). The [worked check](/course-assets/swift/intro-swift-verification-guide.md#mac-setup-and-first-launch-key) distinguishes a preview from a simulator launch. Record which one you observed.
Course Roadmap.Intro to Swift App Development Module Al: In SW8, [Media Gallery App](/courses#intro-to-swift-app-development-sw8-media-maps-and-permission-aware-features-intro-to-swift-app-development-sw8-media-maps-and-permission-aware-features-curriculum-project-media-gallery-app) teaches describing bundled artwork. [Map Places App](/courses#intro-to-swift-app-development-sw8-media-maps-and-permission-aware-features-intro-to-swift-app-development-sw8-media-maps-and-permission-aware-features-curriculum-project-map-places-app) teaches how tapping Neighborhood Cafe changes selection and detail. Predict the camera center separately. Both projects can use supplied data with location and photo access denied.
Course Roadmap.Intro to Swift App Development Reference: Use the [Swift language reference](https://docs.swift.org/swift-book/documentation/the-swift-programming-language/thebasics/) for optional values, [SwiftUI model data](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui/model-data) for ownership and [Swift Testing](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/testing) for a model expectation. The [practice case](/course-assets/swift/intro-swift-practice-pack.md#debugging-and-swift-testing-case) supplies blank and whitespace-only rows for testing a save rule.
Course Roadmap.Intro to Swift App Development Prerequis: To implement Map Places in project order, do the Gallery in SW8 and the Hobby navigation project in SW9. Use the SW10 list example for stable row identity, then return to the SW8 map project before completing Simple Tracker. For the SW8 readiness prediction you can trace a supplied row without implementing its list.
Course Roadmap.Intro to Swift App Development Resource: Choose one project and record the source role, files and smallest repeatable input. For [API-Powered Reference App](/courses#intro-to-swift-app-development-sw12-networking-and-data-loading-intro-to-swift-app-development-sw12-networking-and-data-loading-curriculum-project-api-powered-reference-app), find the fixture with two entries, predict the empty result, and use the [practice case](/course-assets/swift/intro-swift-practice-pack.md#networking-and-data-loading-case) to compare malformed JSON with an HTTP failure. Keep the expected and observed responses in separate columns.

Project Practice Guide.Intro to Swift App Development Project L: The seven builds are Welcome Profile, Media Gallery, Multi-Tab Hobby, Map Places, Simple Tracker, API Reference and Publish-Ready Capstone. SW11 extends Simple Tracker with persistence. The five practice projects here are optional variations that reuse earlier workspaces.
Project Practice Guide.Intro to Swift App Development Checkpoin: For each build, record one ordinary action, an empty or absent value, and a failure or recovery appropriate to the feature. In [Simple Tracker App](/courses#intro-to-swift-app-development-sw10-lists-forms-and-crud-intro-to-swift-app-development-sw10-lists-forms-and-crud-curriculum-project-simple-tracker-app), create a row, reject a whitespace-only title, then add a valid row. Record which action changes the count and the ID that survives a toggle.
Project Practice Guide.Intro to Swift App Development Rubric: Evaluate the flow from a fresh launch. Does the visible result match the selected record? Can the user recover after the failed action? Can someone identify the state without color and operate it at large text sizes? Cite a model check or simulator observation for each claim. Mark a prediction as a prediction.
Project Practice Guide.Intro to Swift App Development Capstone: Use the [practice case](/course-assets/swift/intro-swift-practice-pack.md#capstone-build-and-user-testing-case) to define the audience, one primary flow and one non-goal. Record the model owner, navigation, storage or network choice, test and simulator result. Try empty, failure and recovery states, large text and spoken controls. Use the [practice case](/course-assets/swift/intro-swift-practice-pack.md#final-publishing-walkthrough-case) to decide which discrepancy blocks submission.
Project Practice Guide.Practice Project: Habit Tracker: Start from [Simple Tracker App](/courses#intro-to-swift-app-development-sw10-lists-forms-and-crud-intro-to-swift-app-development-sw10-lists-forms-and-crud-curriculum-project-simple-tracker-app). Replace the sample titles with “Stretch” and “Read”. Add a completed-count label derived from the rows. Toggle Stretch, remove Read and add Read again. The count should progress from 0 of 2 to 1 of 2, 1 of 1 and 1 of 2. State which row retained its ID.
Project Practice Guide.Practice Project: Flashcard App: Start from [Functions, Structs, and Enums](/courses#intro-to-swift-app-development-sw5-functions-structs-and-enums-intro-to-swift-app-development-sw5-functions-structs-and-enums-curriculum-core-project-functions-structs-and-enums). Give two fictional cards a question and answer. Show the question first and reveal the answer on a tap. Advance to the second card. Its answer should be hidden even if the first answer was visible. Empty the deck and check that the reveal action is unavailable.
Project Practice Guide.Practice Project: Weather or API Reader: Start from [API-Powered Reference App](/courses#intro-to-swift-app-development-sw12-networking-and-data-loading-intro-to-swift-app-development-sw12-networking-and-data-loading-curriculum-project-api-powered-reference-app) with its bundled entries. Show a result count and a distinct empty message. Use the [practice case](/course-assets/swift/intro-swift-practice-pack.md#networking-and-data-loading-case) to try two entries, an empty array and a malformed response. Retry with the two valid entries. Explain how the user can distinguish zero matches from a decode failure without a live service.
Project Practice Guide.Practice Project: Notes App with Persist: Use [Persist the Simple Tracker App](/courses#intro-to-swift-app-development-sw11-persistence-with-swiftdata-intro-to-swift-app-development-sw11-persistence-with-swiftdata-curriculum-project-pass-persist-the-simple-tracker-app) with fictional note titles. Start with an empty sample store. Save two notes with the same title, delete one by ID and relaunch. With disk storage the other ID should survive. Repeat with a fresh in-memory container and explain the different result.
Project Practice Guide.Practice Project: Multi-screen Personal: Extend [Multi-Tab Hobby App](/courses#intro-to-swift-app-development-sw9-navigation-and-multi-screen-apps-intro-to-swift-app-development-sw9-navigation-and-multi-screen-apps-curriculum-project-multi-tab-hobby-app) with a summary of favorite hobbies on the home screen. Favorite Photo Walk in detail and check both the summary and Favorites tab. Unfavorite it from detail and return. Both views should return to their empty state. Use one owner for the favorites so the two counts agree.

Intro to Swift App Development: Toolchai.Intro to Swift App Development Setup Ass: Choose a stable Xcode version compatible with your Mac using the [Xcode compatibility table](https://developer.apple.com/xcode/system-requirements/). Record the installed Xcode build, Swift language mode, deployment target and simulator runtime. For the Observation and SwiftData exercises, select an iOS 17-or-later target and compatible runtime.
Intro to Swift App Development: Toolchai.Intro to Swift App Development Upgrade R: Before changing Xcode, record a passing step in [Mac Setup and Project Tooling](/courses#intro-to-swift-app-development-sw1-mac-setup-and-first-launch-intro-to-swift-app-development-sw1-mac-setup-and-first-launch-curriculum-core-project-mac-setup-and-project-tooling). Check the new version against the [Xcode compatibility table](https://developer.apple.com/xcode/system-requirements/), repeat the same edit and simulator run, and record any change in target, runtime or result. A successful preview alone does not check the installed app.
Intro to Swift App Development: Toolchai.Intro to Swift App Development Platform: Without an iPhone, run the core projects on an installed simulator. Without a compatible Mac or runtime, use the [practice case](/course-assets/swift/intro-swift-practice-pack.md#simulator-and-device-validation-case) and report the predicted results. Without a distribution account, use the [practice case](/course-assets/swift/intro-swift-practice-pack.md#app-store-connect-and-testflight-case) for the build and tester decisions.
Intro to Swift App Development: Toolchai.Intro to Swift App Development Reproduci: For a reproducible run, record the project, role, source revision, Xcode build, Swift language mode, target, simulator model and OS. Add the action, expected result and observed result. The [shared working record](/course-assets/swift/intro-swift-practice-pack.md#shared-working-record) provides the fields. Use fictional records and omit account or device identifiers.
Intro to Swift App Development: Toolchai.Intro to Swift App Development First-Run: Open the starter in [Mac Setup and Project Tooling](/courses#intro-to-swift-app-development-sw1-mac-setup-and-first-launch-intro-to-swift-app-development-sw1-mac-setup-and-first-launch-curriculum-core-project-mac-setup-and-project-tooling), select the FirstLaunch app scheme and an installed iPhone simulator, and run it. Look for “Ready to launch”. In ContentView.swift change the title argument to “First verified launch”. Stop and run again. Record the heading in the launched app and the destination.
Intro to Swift App Development: Toolchai.Intro to Swift App Development Version D: Compare your Xcode build and macOS version with the [Xcode compatibility table](https://developer.apple.com/xcode/system-requirements/). In the [practice case](/course-assets/swift/intro-swift-practice-pack.md#mac-setup-and-first-launch-case), the preview shows edited text while the simulator shows old text. Check the selected scheme, target membership and run destination before attributing the difference to the SDK. Record one changed variable and repeat the launch.
